note: Arc library. Arcs are starting structures: a project may use a subset or reorder stages and records why in beatmap.arc.notes. Add an arc by appending an entry; nothing else changes.

arcs.name: Question -> investigation -> revelation
best_for: explainers built on a surprising fact

stages.guidance: Open on the question as an image or a contradiction, not as a sentence read aloud.
Show the tools: what is measured, compared, ruled out. Each clue changes the picture.
Spend the biggest visual move here; the answer should be seen before it is explained.
What the answer changes. End smaller than the reveal.

arcs.pitfall: Posing a question the narration answers in the next sentence; no investigation means no tension.

arcs.name: Chronological progression

stages.guidance: Place and time as a concrete scene.
Pick 3-5 turning points, not every date; each gets a distinct visual setting.
The event the sequence was building toward.
What remained; link back to the present.

arcs.pitfall: A date list. A timeline is a structure, not a story; each step needs a cause.

arcs.name: Problem -> mechanism -> consequence

stages.guidance: Make the failure or gap felt before it is explained.
Reveal how it works spatially and over time; this is where diagrams earn their place.
Show the outcome at human or system scale.
What changes, or what remains unresolved.

arcs.pitfall: Mechanism told in words over a static diagram; the mechanism must move.

arcs.name: Parallel narratives

stages.guidance: First thread, with its own visual world.
Second thread; deliberately different palette or camera so the viewer can tell them apart.
Alternate with shortening intervals; match-cut across threads.
Threads meet; unify the visual language at last.
What the pairing shows that neither did alone.

arcs.pitfall: Interleaving without a reason; the cut between threads needs a rhyme (shape, motion, sound).

arcs.name: Cause and effect

stages.guidance: The first domino, concrete and small.
Each link visibly causes the next; reuse one motion across links so the chain reads as one system.
The link where scale changes.
The end state against the starting state.

arcs.pitfall: Links that are only asserted. Each causal step needs a visible transfer.

arcs.name: Journey of discovery

stages.guidance: Leave the familiar; establish scale.
Move through layers; camera does the narrating.
The thing at the end of the journey.
Bring the viewer back with a changed view of the start.

arcs.pitfall: A journey with no destination; or camera moves unconnected to meaning.

arcs.name: Documentary investigation

stages.guidance: The event, documented.
Sources on screen: documents, records, figures. Cite visually.
What does not fit.
State what is established and what is not.
Why it matters.

arcs.pitfall: Evidence shown as decoration; if a source appears it must be legible and attributable.

arcs.name: Visual metaphor-driven

stages.guidance: Introduce the metaphor as an object or place.
Map each part of the metaphor to a part of the idea, one at a time.
Push the metaphor until it shows the idea's limit or failure case.
Let the metaphor resolve; name the idea plainly once.

arcs.pitfall: A decorative metaphor that is never mapped to the claim, or one pushed past where it is true.

arcs.name: Hook -> context -> build -> payoff -> wrap

stages.guidance: Within the first seconds: a surprising fact, mistake or question as a visual.
Only what the build needs.
Two or three steps, each with a changed picture.
Deliver on the hook.
One line, then stop.

arcs.pitfall: Hook that the payoff does not answer.

arcs.name: Problem -> agitate -> solve

stages.guidance: A specific pain.
Make the cost of the problem concrete.
The solution performing, not described.
Evidence the solution works.
One clear next step.

arcs.pitfall: Unsupported claims in the proof stage.

arcs.name: Before -> after -> bridge

stages.guidance: The old state, concrete.
The new state, same framing so the difference is readable.
How to get from one to the other.

arcs.pitfall: Different framings for before and after; the comparison loses its force.

arcs.name: Man in hole (fall and recovery)

stages.guidance: What normal looks like.
The drop.
Stay in the low point long enough to feel it.
What changed to start recovery.
The new normal.

arcs.pitfall: A fall that is only a line going down; the trough needs its own scene.

arcs.name: Hook -> stake -> body -> payoff -> loop (reel length)
best_for: reel-type portrait films of 45-60 s (45 s preferred; the type allows 30-75 s)
one idea with one surprising fact or number

stages.guidance: 0-2 s. The claim, with the hero object already on screen and the hook card up at frame 1. No greeting, no title, no logo. Spoken line and on-screen line are written separately (the card is 6 words or fewer).
2-7 s. Why this matters to the person watching, in one line. Only what the body needs.
One idea per beat and a different picture every beat, with a different object each time rather than one template repeated. If the script holds two ideas, it is two films.
The last 3-5 s. Deliver exactly what the hook promised, with the biggest visual move of the film.
The last line echoes one word or image from the hook so a replay lands clean. End on one action or none, never two.

arcs.pitfall: A hook the payoff does not answer, or a loop line that is only a sign-off. Under 7 s there is no room for a stake. 45 s is the preferred length; stretch to 60 s only when a complicated topic needs more animated beats, and add a mid-film re-hook; for a long-reel (60-180 s) or youtube video use another arc.
